notes.text: Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games.

Mike Matheson is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Noah Dobson has taken his spot beside Kaiden Guhle. That pair has had 37% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 48:24 together, down from 54% with Matheson.
Dylan Larkin was added to the roster on Nov 24 and has played beside Alexandre Texier and Alex Newhook.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 24 games, up from 6% last season.
Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Nelson has taken his spot beside Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas.
Mike Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 16.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

COL.head: Leaning the Avalanche’s way
COL.body: Even though Colorado will be without MacKinnon, the Avalanche have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Suzuki’s favorite opponent
paras: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Montréal on Nov 14. The Canadiens (14-7-4) lost 2-1 to Los Angeles on Monday, while the Avs (13-7-3) beat Anaheim 4-0 on Thursday. Two good teams meet. Going in, the Canadiens are third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 11th).

The Canadiens’ record (.640) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.552), largely because they’re 9-7 in one-goal games. The Avalanche’s record (.630) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (30th). The Avalanche get their defensemen shooting (1st), do a lot of their shooting from distance (most) and play the league’s fastest games (1st). Colorado has scored 3.91 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Avalanche keep dangerous shots away, but the Canadiens give up a lot of them.

Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 25 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 25 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Avalanche, Martin Nečas (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (15 G / 6 A / 21 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, sixth in the NHL.
Jacob Fowler (10-3-2 / .918 SV% in 15 GS) has been terrific for Montréal and is expected to start. Mackenzie Blackwood (11-4-1 / .904 SV% in 16 GS) is expected to go for Colorado.

items.text: Nick Suzuki has a point in seven straight games against Colorado.
The Canadiens have been without Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Mike Matheson for several games.

The Avalanche have been without Nathan MacKinnon since Nov 12. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Capitals and the Mammoth are missing more right now.
Cale Makar has missed the Avalanche’s last three games.
